body:
## Summary

start-command 0.38.0 detects a Docker daemon restart (`Exit evidence: docker-daemon-restart`, `exitReason: killed (docker daemon restart)`, from #194) only with `journalctl -u docker.service`. When `$` runs inside a container that reaches the host daemon through a mounted `/var/run/docker.sock` (Docker-outside-of-Docker, which is how the hive-mind Telegram bot runs), `DOCKER_HOST` is unset, so the check counts as "local". But the container has no host journal, so the probe finds nothing, and a task killed by a daemon restart ends with `Exit evidence: unavailable`.

Found while fixing [link-assistant/hive-mind#2892](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2892) (a daemon restart reported as an OOM kill).

## Evidence (0.38.0 package source)

`src/lib/exit-evidence.js`:

- Lines 68-70: `local` is true when `DOCKER_HOST` is unset or `unix://…`, which includes a mounted host socket.
- Lines 80-96: the only daemon-restart evidence is `journalctl -u docker.service --since <FinishedAt-60s> --until <FinishedAt+1s>`.
- Lines 99-114: the socket-based fallback (`docker events`) only looks for `event=oom`.
- Line 131: otherwise it returns `Exit evidence: unavailable (no attributed exit-time OOM or daemon restart evidence)`.

## Reproduction (expected from the code above; not yet run end to end)

1. Start a container with the host socket mounted and start-command installed: `docker run -it -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock <image-with-$>`.
2. Inside it: `$ --isolated docker --detached --image alpine:3.20 -- sleep 600`.
3. On the host (with `"live-restore": false`): `sudo systemctl restart docker`. dockerd force-kills the task (`using the force`, exit 137).
4. Back in the container: `$ --status <id>`. Exit evidence is `unavailable`, and no `killed (docker daemon restart)` reason is given. The same steps run on the host give `docker-daemon-restart`.

## Expected

The same attribution with or without host journal access, using only what the Docker API exposes over the socket.

## Workaround in hive-mind

hive-mind adds its own checks (`src/docker-daemon-restart.lib.mjs`). Its strongest socket-only check is a burst test: the bot's own container (`docker inspect $HOSTNAME`) also exited within ±15 s of the task's `FinishedAt` and was started again after it. Two unrelated containers dying in the same second points at the daemon, not at one task's cgroup.

## Suggested fix

When the journal is unavailable or empty, add Docker-API evidence:

- other containers whose `State.FinishedAt` is within a few seconds of this one, with exit 137 or 143, and without an `oom` event;
- containers whose `State.StartedAt` (restart policy) comes after that `FinishedAt`, which means the daemon came back.

`docker events` cannot be used for this, because the event buffer does not survive a daemon restart. `State.FinishedAt` and `State.StartedAt` do survive it.

Report which source supported the attribution (journal or API), and add a test with stubbed `docker inspect` / `docker ps -a` output for two containers that finished in the same second.
title: Daemon-restart exit evidence needs the host journal: with a mounted docker.sock (DooD) a daemon-restart kill is 'Exit evidence: unavailable'
